sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Colonial Land Revenue Policy**: The shift from traditional revenue collection to **fixed cash-based revenue** forced peasants into the clutches of moneylenders.
• **Commercialization of Agriculture**: Forced shift from subsistence crops to **cash crops** (indigo, cotton, jute) made peasants vulnerable to global market fluctuations.
• **De-industrialization**: The collapse of rural handicrafts forced artisans back to land, increasing **pressure on land** and leading to land fragmentation.
• **Institutional Exploitation**: The **Zamindari system** empowered intermediaries to extract 'abwabs' (illegal cesses) and perform arbitrary evictions.

items.definition: Illegal cesses or arbitrary taxes levied by landlords over and above the fixed rent, a primary cause of peasant unrest.
A legislative response to the Deccan Riots, aimed at curbing the power of moneylenders and protecting peasant landholdings.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Legal Resistance**: Use of the court system to challenge illegal evictions (e.g., Pabna Agrarian League).
• **Social Boycott**: Non-violent resistance against oppressive landlords (e.g., Eka Movement).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of unified leadership, regional isolation, and brutal state suppression.
• **Solutions**: Emergence of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936) to provide a national platform.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'R-E-A-L' (Reasons for Resistance)
• **Decoded Meaning**: R-Revenue (High taxes), E-Eviction (Land insecurity), A-Abwabs (Illegal cesses), L-Lender (Debt trap).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Peasant Movements' with 'Tribal Movements'. Remember: Peasant movements were primarily against economic exploitation (rent/debt), while tribal movements were against cultural/territorial encroachment.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Agrarian Distress' to link historical peasant movements with contemporary agricultural policy debates.

keyTakeaways: Peasant movements were not anti-British initially but anti-landlord/moneylender.
The transition from 'local grievances' to 'national consciousness' occurred post-1920s.
Legislative interventions like the Deccan Agriculturists Relief Act were reactive, not proactive.
